players.product: Aurora sodium fast-reactor SMR powerhouses for data-center power (1.2 GW Ohio campus for Meta; Aurora-INL 2028 startup)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (pre-revenue): net loss of $33.1 million (loss from operations of $51.2 million and income tax expense of $3.2 million, offset by $21.3 million of net interest and dividend income); cash used in operating activities of $17.9 million; capital spend of $32.8 million on planned property, plant and equipment across all three business units. Ended the quarter with cash and marketable securities of $2.5 billion, including the additional $1.2 billion of capital generated in the first quarter from the completion of the ATM program.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 net loss $33.1 million; capital spend $32.8 million; cash and marketable securities $2.5 billion; $1.2 billion from ATM completion

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance as stated on the Q1 call (CFO: 'We are trending toward our guided ranges'): cash used in operating activities of $80 million-$100 million and cash used in investing activities for the deployment of property, plant, and equipment of $350 million-$450 million, reflecting deployment across power, fuel and isotopes; management expects to accelerate procurement and construction through the year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 operating cash use $80 million-$100 million; PP&E deployment $350 million-$450 million

quarterly_data.signal: Aurora-INL (first Aurora powerhouse) status: DOE Other Transaction Agreement executed and Nuclear Safety Design Agreement approved; Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis (PDSA) submitted and in review, with DSA approval, readiness review and startup approval as next milestones. NRC approved the Principal Design Criteria Topical Report in parallel. On site, field execution is transitioning to deep foundation excavation; long lead procurement is advancing across major systems and supplier engagement is progressing for the reactor module and balance of plant. CEO expects the proposed NRC Part 57 to be the platform used 'most likely for most of our plants going forward and most likely to convert the Aurora-INL'.

Aurora Ohio (1.2 gigawatt campus planned with Meta): Oklo submitted PJM interconnection applications as part of the most recent cluster study, described as key to site development and deployment timelines; CFO said the interconnection turnaround is 'measured in, you know, months if not more than a year' and is disconnected from the nuclear regulatory process. CEO cited PJM's need for new firm supply, including bridging 'a potential 50-60 gigawatt capacity shortfall over the next decade', as support for co-located, campus-style deployment serving large loads.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.2 gigawatt Ohio campus; PJM 50-60 gigawatt capacity shortfall cited

quarterly_data.signal: Fuel strategy (fuel called 'one of the most important gating items for advanced nuclear deployment'): Oklo is working with enrichers including longtime partner Centrus and says 'We're seeing timescales and delivery schedules shift to the left for the first time.' Government surplus materials (down-blended HEU and surplus plutonium) are emerging as a bridge fuel; the government's first tranche of 20 tons of plutonium is 'equivalent to, you know, between 160 to 200 tons of HALEU'. Ohio plants would start on fresh fuel plus government sources, then refuel with commercial HALEU until recycling comes online. A3F fuel fabrication facility at INL: NSDA and PDSA approved, early construction activities complete, final design deliverables complete, next milestone the construction contract award.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 tons plutonium first tranche equivalent to 160 to 200 tons of HALEU

quarterly_data.signal: Aurora Eielson: Defense Logistics Agency Energy, on behalf of the Department of the Air Force, issued a Notice of Intent to award to Oklo for an Aurora-derived cogeneration powerhouse at Eielson Air Force Base in Alaska, planned to deliver at least 5 MW of electric power with steam for district heating as the primary use; CEO described it as a 60 MW thermal plant using the same fuel form and, in many cases, the same vendors as the Aurora product line (which is 'focused on the sort of, you know, 35 MW plus data center side'). Site characterization is ongoing with ground investigations expected this summer; the intended licensing path is Part 57.
quarterly_data.figure: at least 5 MW electric; 60 MW thermal

quarterly_data.signal: NRC Part 57 (proposed): designed for faster, repeatable deployment of microreactors and smaller advanced reactors with fleet-based licensing; the NRC has discussed targeted licensing and deployment timelines of 6-12 months. CEO understands it could be usable 'as soon as later this year' after the public comment period, aligning with Oklo's multi-powerhouse, campus-style fleet model.

Financing: CFO said Oklo has been active in capital markets 'to make sure that capital is not a constraint for our asset deployment timeline' and is now exploring government financing and asset-level financing options, which 'could even include supplier financing', as ways to lower cost of capital and accelerate deployment rather than as something required.

Isotopes: the Idaho Radiochemistry Laboratory (NRC Material Handling Permit received earlier this year) has its first commercial isotope contract pending with an unnamed customer and is working toward early commercial isotope revenue starting in 2026; the Groves isotope test reactor was targeting criticality by July 4, 2026 at the time of the call.
quarterly_data.figure: early commercial isotope revenue starting in 2026; Groves criticality target July 4, 2026

contracts.signal: Meta and Oklo announced plans earlier this year to develop a 1.2 gigawatt advanced nuclear power campus in Ohio; this quarter Oklo submitted PJM interconnection applications for the campus as part of the most recent cluster study and continues permitting, site-readiness and stakeholder work. Fuel for the Ohio plants would come from fresh fuel plus government sources, transitioning to commercial HALEU refueling.
